short: A traditional shanty also called Eliza Lee.
note: A work song also known as Clear the Track, Let the Bulgine Run or Eliza Lee. Collected versions were sung while turning a ship’s capstan or windlass; its verses vary between singers.

sources.label: Smithsonian Folkways: Clear the Track, Let the Bulgine Run

short: An old slang word for a steam engine.
note: A nineteenth-century slang term for an engine, especially a steam engine, familiar from traditional work songs.

sources.label: Kipling Society: Steam Tactics, annotation to bulgine

short: A ship making regular scheduled voyages.
note: A packet ship carries mail, passengers, or goods on a regular route. The name comes from the packets of letters such vessels originally transported.

short: A long, inexpensive cigar.
note: A long, thin, inexpensive cigar. The name is shortened from Conestoga, the Pennsylvania place-name also associated with the heavy covered wagons whose drivers smoked them.

short: A one-eyed giant of Greek mythology.
note: A Cyclops is a giant with a single eye in the middle of its forehead. Greek traditions include the divine smiths who make Zeus’s thunderbolts and Polyphemus, whom Odysseus encounters.

short: A. A. Milne’s toy bear of the Hundred Acre Wood.
note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the bear in A. A. Milne’s children’s books, beginning with Winnie-the-Pooh (1926). His home bears a name-board reading Sanders, so he literally lives beneath that name.

short: A wise man, magician, or member of the ancient Magi.
note: Latin magus, from Greek magos, originally denoted a member of a Persian priestly group. In later use it can mean an astrologer, sorcerer, or learned magician.

short: The refrain of the traditional song Good Morning Blues.
note: Good Morning Blues is a traditional blues song recorded by Lead Belly. It addresses the blues as a visitor and asks how it is doing.

sources.label: Smithsonian Folkways: Lead Belly, Good Morning Blues

short: A traditional ballad of impossible courtship tasks.
note: Strawberry Lane is a variant of the ballad family usually called The Elfin Knight, which also includes Scarborough Fair. A would-be lover is set seemingly impossible tasks, such as making a shirt without needlework.

sources.label: University of Tennessee: Strawberry Lane, collected in Folk Songs of North America
Durham University: traditional ballads, Strawberry Lane under Child 2

short: An American refrain urging people to fend for themselves.
note: The saying tells a hog to root for its own food or perish: make a living by your own efforts. It became a recurring refrain in nineteenth-century American songs, including songs of ox-team drivers.

sources.label: Library of Congress: Ozark folk-song collections
Library of Congress: Root, Hog, or Die (1856)

short: The curved wooden piece of an ox’s yoke.
note: A U-shaped wooden bow fitted under an ox’s neck and secured to the yoke. The term also gives its name to a similarly shaped bend in a river.

short: Shenandoah, the American folk song.
note: Shenandoah is a traditional American song with widely varying lyrics and an uncertain early history. Many familiar versions include a refrain about crossing the wide Missouri River.

short: A familiar nickname for the Missouri River.
note: The Missouri River earned this nickname from the heavy loads of sediment in its water. It joins the Mississippi, which carries their combined flow to the Gulf of Mexico.

sources.label: National Park Service: Missouri River and tributaries

short: A traditional American spiritual about a traveler’s heavenly home.
note: Often called Poor Wayfaring Stranger, this spiritual presents earthly life as a difficult journey toward a home beyond suffering and separation. It has circulated widely in folk and gospel singing.

sources.label: Smithsonian Folkways: Pete Seeger, The Wayfaring Stranger

short: The Irish melody later used for Danny Boy.
note: An untitled air supplied by Jane Ross of Limavady appeared in George Petrie’s Ancient Music of Ireland in 1855. Usually called the Londonderry Air, it was later paired with the words of Danny Boy.

sources.label: Trinity College Dublin Library: Irish folk music

aliases: The minstrel boy to the war is gone
short: Thomas Moore’s song about a musician going to war.
note: A lyric from Thomas Moore’s Irish Melodies. Its young harpist goes to battle, and the song associates his instrument with freedom and resistance to servitude.

short: A lyric from Thomas Moore’s Irish Melodies.
note: Moore addresses a silent harp whose music is bound to sorrow and lost freedom. Images of a dying swan and flowers mixed with chains explain why it cannot supply cheerful songs.

short: Calm, peaceful, or idyllic.
note: Originally a legendary bird identified with the kingfisher, believed to nest on the sea while it was calm. Halcyon days consequently came to mean a period of tranquility or happiness.

short: Lewis Carroll’s creature named after imitation turtle soup.
note: The Mock Turtle appears in Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland (1865). Its calf-like features play on mock turtle soup, traditionally made with calf’s head as a substitute for turtle meat.

sources.label: Lewis Carroll: Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland

short: The railroad engineer immortalized in an American ballad.
note: John Luther “Casey” Jones (1864–1900) was an Illinois Central engineer killed in a train collision at Vaughan, Mississippi. Songs about his fatal run made him a figure of American railway folklore.

sources.label: National Museum of American History: Casey Jones’s grave marker
Library of Congress: The Folklore and Folksong of Trains in America

short: A sailing ship built for speed.
note: A fast sailing ship, especially the slender, heavily canvassed merchant ships of the nineteenth century.

short: An instrument that displays changing electrical signals.
note: An electronic instrument that graphs a signal’s changing amplitude against time, making rapid variations visible on a screen.

short: A plucked instrument with strings stretched from a crossbar.
note: A stringed instrument with two arms supporting a crossbar above a soundbox. Ancient Greek lyres accompanied songs and recitations.

short: A small plucked instrument of the lute family.
note: A fretted stringed instrument usually having four pairs of strings tuned in fifths and played with a pick.

short: Tones at whole-number multiples of a fundamental frequency.
note: A harmonic has a frequency that is a whole-number multiple of a fundamental tone. The higher harmonics are overtones that contribute to a musical sound’s character.

short: A harp whose pedals alter the strings’ pitches.
note: The modern concert harp normally has forty-seven strings and seven foot pedals. Each pedal alters the pitch of all strings belonging to one note-name.

term: I’m broke and I ain’t got a dime
aliases: Mama don’t treat your daughter mean
short: A verse from the One Dime Blues tradition.
note: These floating blues verses occur in the tradition of One Dime Blues, recorded by Blind Lemon Jefferson in 1927 and subsequently adapted by other singers.

sources.label: Smithsonian Folkways: Lead Belly, Shout On liner notes
Smithsonian Folkways: Virginia Traditions, Karo Street Blues liner notes

short: Improvising without advance preparation.
note: To compose or perform spontaneously rather than follow something fully prepared beforehand.

short: The main body of an aircraft.
note: The central body of an aircraft, containing such spaces as the cockpit, passenger compartment, and cargo hold.
